# Evaluation limits. Cases keep a wide margin: the exact step count is
# implementation-defined, only the fact that a runaway script stops is not.

=== infinite recursion stops on the step limit
limits steps=100
(let () (def loop (fn (n) (loop n))) (loop 0))
--- error
--- at 1:28
--- message step limit exceeded

=== infinite recursion stops on the recursion limit
limits recursion=5
(let () (def loop (fn (n) (loop n))) (loop 0))
--- error
--- at 1:27
--- message recursion limit exceeded

=== deep recursion fails under a small recursion limit
limits recursion=5
(let () (def f (fn (n) (if (= n 0) 0 (f (- n 1))))) (f 50))
--- error
--- at 1:38
--- message recursion limit exceeded

=== the same recursion succeeds with the default limits
(let () (def f (fn (n) (if (= n 0) 0 (f (- n 1))))) (f 50))
--- want
0

=== a long loop fails under a small step limit
limits steps=50
(fold (fn (acc x) (+ acc x)) 0 (range 100))
--- error
--- at 1:19
--- message step limit exceeded

=== the same loop succeeds with the default limits
(fold (fn (acc x) (+ acc x)) 0 (range 100))
--- want
4950

=== limits reset between runs
limits steps=100000
(fold (fn (acc x) (+ acc x)) 0 (range 100))
--- want
4950

=== range beyond the element ceiling is an error
(range 1e18)
--- error
--- at 1:1
--- message range expects integer bounds, got 0 and 1e+18

=== range with a huge negative start is an error
(range -1e18 0)
--- error
--- at 1:1
--- message range expects integer bounds, got -1e+18 and 0

=== range with bounds past the integers a number holds is an error
(range -9e18 9e18)
--- error
--- at 1:1
--- message range expects integer bounds, got -9e+18 and 9e+18

# A list or a tuple may hold the same value more than once: a value made in
# a few steps can be small in memory and far too large to walk. Writing it
# and comparing it stop at 262144 parts and 512 levels, in every runtime: a
# ceiling measured on what writing it costs, a number at a time.

=== a shared value too large to write is an error
(let ((v (fold (fn (a x) (tuple a a)) 0 (range 30))))
  (string v))
--- error
--- at 2:3
--- message value too large: more than 262144 parts

=== a shared value too large to compare is an error
(let ((v (fold (fn (a x) (tuple a a)) 0 (range 30))))
  (= v v))
--- error
--- at 2:3
--- message value too large: more than 262144 parts

=== a list of 262143 items is 262144 parts: at the ceiling, it compares
(= (range 262143) (range 262143))
--- want
#t

=== one item more is past the ceiling
(= (range 262144) (range 262144))
--- error
--- at 1:1
--- message value too large: more than 262144 parts

=== a value too deep to compare is an error
(let ((v (fold (fn (a x) (list a)) 0 (range 600))))
  (= v v))
--- error
--- at 2:3
--- message value too deep: more than 512 levels

=== a comparison settled early walks no further
(let ((v (fold (fn (a x) (tuple a a)) 0 (range 30))))
  (list (= v (tuple)) (= v (tuple 0 0)) (!= v (tuple 1))))
--- want
(list #f #f #t)

=== a shared value under the ceiling compares
(let ((v (fold (fn (a x) (tuple a a)) 0 (range 10))))
  (= v v))
--- want
#t
